newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran radio urges boycott of U.S. goods over Israel.
newsitem.headline: Iran radio urges boycott of U.S. goods over Israel.

text.p: Iranian state radio said on Wednesday a boycott of U.S. goods by Islamic states would be an effective way of forcing Washington to stop supporting Israel.

"A prevalent method which is both practical and possible would be for Islamic states and other peoples of the world to set up an economic embargo on the Zionist regime (Israel) and a boycott of goods from America as this regime's unconditional supporter," state-run Tehran radio said in a commentary.
"Using this method could pressure this country (U.S.) to decrease its support of Tel Aviv by raising the prospect that America's economic standing in the world could be jeopardised," the radio added.

It was commenting on a session of the U.N. General Assembly on Wednesday summoned at the request of Arab states in reaction to the vetoing by the United States last Friday of a resolution in the Security Council calling on Israel to abandon plans for a new Jewish neighbourhood in mainly Arab East Jerusalem.

The United States, like the almost 50 other speakers in the council debate, was critical of the Israeli action but said the U.N. body was not an appropriate forum for dealing with issues under negotiation between the two parties.
Iran has strongly condemned the U.S. veto and urged world action against the Israeli plan to build Jewish housing in East Jerusalem, the site of Islam's third holiest shrine.
